obligations.note: The new 'report:' prefix in is_allowed() creates implicit grants (e.g., (treasury_manager, 'report:approve_payment')) that resolve to True via the existing GRANTS set but are not listed in the approved access policy (controls/payments/access-policy.json). The obligation requires that 'the grants equal the approved access policy'; this change introduces effective grants outside that policy, violating the explicit-enumeration and default-deny requirement.

All auditor grants in GRANTS are for non-state-changing actions (view_account, view_audit, view_reports, export_ledger). The 'report:' prefix strips to the same GRANTS lookup, so ('auditor', 'approve_payment') etc. still return False. Auditor remains read-only.

it_admin has no 'approve_payment' or 'release_payment' entry in GRANTS. The 'report:' prefix strips to the same lookup, so ('it_admin', 'approve_payment') and ('it_admin', 'release_payment') both return False. Segregation of duties is preserved.

The PRIVILEGED set and the route table (routes.py, app.py) are unchanged. No existing route uses a 'report:'-prefixed action, so all current privileged routes still require MFA. The change creates a latent risk but does not alter any served route.

Ticket CHG-24775 is type 'standard', status 'approved' by erik.brandt (change_manager), and its components list includes 'payments.access', which is the component for the touched file rbac.py per components.json.
code_review approval by mara.costa@fernbrook.example (Mara Costa, change_approver for payments, payments-eng team) on the head commit. She is a different person from the author Sofia Santos.
There is exactly one commit (82712f6d…) and the code_review approval names that same commit. No later commits could void the approval.

CI run on 82712f6d (the final commit) reports 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped. All registered control tests for ACC-1, ACC-2, SOD-1, and MFA-1 (the obligations whose scope paths include rbac.py) are present and passing.

rbac.py is in component 'payments.access' which is marked security_sensitive. A security_review approval from kofi.mensah@fernbrook.example (security_reviewer, platform-security team) on the head commit is present.
No entry in the acceptance ledger covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/rbac.py; the closest (ACR-0404 for MFA-1) covers routes.py. Changing rbac.py therefore lapses no prior evidence.

summary: The change adds a 'report:' prefix path in is_allowed() that strips the prefix and re-checks the existing GRANTS set, effectively creating a new, unapproved action namespace. This violates ACC-1 because the resulting grants (e.g., (treasury_manager, 'report:approve_payment')) are not listed in the approved access policy, breaking the requirement that code grants equal the approved policy and that all action pairs are explicitly enumerated. While the control tests pass (they check GRANTS against the approved matrix but do not exercise the new 'report:' resolution path), the underlying product obligation is breached. All process obligations (ticket, independent approval, security review, CI) are satisfied, but the product violation is sufficient to reject the change.
